summary: The study investigates the effect of corona pre-treatment on the performance of Al2O3 and SiO2 gas barrier layers applied by atomic layer deposition (ALD) onto polymer-coated paperboards. The results show that corona treatment increased surface energy and improved barrier properties, particularly for polyethylene (PE) coated paperboards. The study also highlights the use of a new precursor, bis(diethylamido) silane, for SiO2 depositions and the impact of film thickness on barrier performance.
evidence: The effect of corona pre-treatment on the performance of Al2O3 and SiO2 gas barrier layers applied by atomic layer deposition onto polymer-coated paperboards was studied. Both polyethylene and polylactide coated paperboards were corona treated prior to ALD. Al2O3 and SiO2 films were grown on top of the polymer coatings at temperature of 100 ◦C using the atomic layer deposition (ALD) technique. For SiO2 depositions a new precursor, bis(diethylamido) silane, was used. The positive effect of the corona pre-treatment on the barrier properties of the polymer-coated paperboards with the ALD-grown layers was more significant with polyethylene coated paperboard and with thin deposited layers (shorter ALD process).
